searchText: Question: if I'm correct, EOFCREATE is used by EOAs to deploy an EOF contract and RETURNCONTRACT is used by EOF contracts to deploy EOF contracts, right? No. EOFCREATE/RETURNCONTRACT are used by contracts to create other contracts. EOAs use the contract creation transacion like they would in legacy, with some variations described in EIP-7698 to support constructor parameters in solidity and vyper. Okay? I think I get it now. EOFCREATE is the opcode the deployer contract calls to create the contract and RETURNCONTRACT is the opcode the init code uses to return the runtime code, yes? Yes, creating a contract is a two step process. EOFCREATE starts it within a contract and in both EOFCREATE or creation transaciton the RETURNCONTRACT call returns the contract. What differes is how you trigger the initcode step. Got it thanks! hey guys, where can we find Eof tests suites ? Here's latest release: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/releases/tag/eip7692%40v1.0.3 And source and all implemented test source code can be found here: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/tree/main/tests/prague/eip7692_eof_v1 In yellow paper, it is stated `0xfe INVALID ∅ ∅ Designated invalid instruction.` This should be `0xEF` right? Found explanation. 0xFE was marked as INVALID here: https://github.com/ethereum/yellowpaper/pull/230 Yea, 0xFE has been used as a zero-data revert. EF is an unallocated opcode so it also triggers an exceptional halt like FE, but 0xFE is explicitly reserved for this.

excerpts.author: michaelamadi
excerpts.content: Question: if I'm correct, EOFCREATE is used by EOAs to deploy an EOF contract and RETURNCONTRACT is used by EOF contracts to deploy EOF contracts, right?

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: No.  EOFCREATE/RETURNCONTRACT are used by contracts to create other contracts.  EOAs use the contract creation transacion like they would in legacy, with some variations described in EIP-7698 to support constructor parameters in solidity and vyper.

excerpts.author: michaelamadi
excerpts.content: Okay? I think I get it now. EOFCREATE is the opcode the deployer contract calls to create the contract and RETURNCONTRACT is the opcode the init code uses to return the runtime code, yes?

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: Yes, creating a contract is a two step process.  EOFCREATE starts it within a contract and in both EOFCREATE or creation transaciton the RETURNCONTRACT call returns the contract.  What differes is how you trigger the initcode step.
